BASIC floating-point workspace: the tail of FAC2's mantissa ($6B-$6D), its sign ($6E), the
FAC1/FAC2 sign comparison ($6F), FAC1's rounding byte ($70), and FBUFPT ($71-$72), a series
evaluation pointer still holding $A30A inside BASIC ROM. Inherited state; the game's own
zero-page allocation ends at $6A (SAVED_PARSE_INDEX).

CHRGET ($0073-$008A) - executable code living in zero page, not data.
The KERNAL copies this 24-byte routine into RAM at power-up; it is BASIC's tokenizer feed. It
increments the 16-bit text pointer at $7A/$7B, fetches the next program byte through an
absolute LDA whose operand IS $7A/$7B (self-modifying by design), skips spaces, and returns
with carry clear when the byte is an ASCII digit.
Byte-verified against the stock routine:
E6 7A D0 02 E6 7B AD 06 02 C9 3A B0 0A C9 20 F0 EF 38 E9 30 38 E9 D0 60
Unmodified and unreachable here: BASIC ROM is banked out ($01 = $36). TXTPTR reads $0206,
pointing into the BASIC input buffer - residue of the RUN that started the game.

RNDX ($8B-$8F) - BASIC's RND seed, still the stock power-up value 80 4F C7 52 58. The game
never uses BASIC's generator.

KERNAL I/O status and scratch ($90-$B1): STATUS ($90) = $40, the EOI left by the last LOAD;

and 3, the default keyboard input and screen output devices; TIME ($A0-$A2), the software

never calls UDTIM; and tape/RS-232 temporaries the game never uses. SAL ($AC-$AD) and EAL
($AE-$AF) are the start and end addresses of the last KERNAL LOAD.

KERNAL screen-editor, keyboard and RS-232 workspace ($C7-$FD). The game reads or writes none of it except $FD; the values are stale state from before the program took the machine over, and they are internally consistent for a stock 40x25 screen at $0400. The game own screen is SCREEN_RAM at $CC00.
$CB SFDX is the matrix code of the key being scanned; $40 means none. $CC BLNSW disables cursor blink. $D1-$D2 point to screen line $0400. $D5 LNMX is $27 (39). $D6 TBLX is the cursor physical line and is not game state. $D9-$F2 is the 26-byte screen line-link table. $F3-$F4 point to Color RAM $D800; $F5-$F6 point to the KERNAL unshifted keyboard table $EB81; $F7-$FA are null RS-232 buffer pointers. $FD is cleared by LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART at $971B with the KERNAL file parameters; its consumer is the fast-loader image under I/O at $DC00-$DFFF, outside this snapshot.
Ghidra 6502 SLEIGH models JSR, RTS, PHA and PLA stack accesses at $00Fx rather than $01Fx, producing roughly 189 false references into $F0-$F9. The only real game access here is $971B writing $FD. The modeled stack traffic nevertheless establishes that the live stack did not descend below $01F0, explaining why the excluded prior-stage bytes at $0100-$01E8 survive unchanged in this later gameplay snapshot.

KERNAL LDTB1 ($D9-$F2) — the screen editor's 26-byte line-link table: one entry per screen row
plus an editor scratch byte. Bits 0-3 hold the screen-memory page displacement of that row's
first byte; bit 7 set marks the first physical line of a logical line. The captured $84/$85/$86/
$87 pattern describes a stock 40x25 screen based at $0400, i.e. state left over from before the
game took the machine. The game neither reads nor writes it; the incoming references are the
6502 stack-modelling artifact described in the KERNAL_EDITOR_WORKSPACE plate at $C7.

KEYBOARD_BUFFER (KEYD, $0277-$0280) - the KERNAL's ten-byte keystroke FIFO.
SCNKEY ($FF9F) scans the keyboard matrix through CIA 1 and appends PETSCII codes here,
bumping the count in NDX ($00C6); GETIN ($FFE4) removes the oldest code and decrements NDX.
The fill limit is XMAX ($0289), default 10.
This program never touches the buffer directly, but it is squarely on the input path: $0552
and $084B call SCNKEY, $0555 and $084E call GETIN, and $083A zeroes NDX to flush pending
keystrokes before reading a command line. Empty at capture.

CLRCHN, CHRIN, CHROUT, STOP, GETIN, CLALL, the user command, LOAD and SAVE.
Every one is at its ROM default for KERNAL revision 901227-03 ($F34A, $F291, $F20E, $F250,

table (SETNAM $FFBD and friends) and lets the KERNAL run normally.
Note Mapping the 64 lists ILOAD/ISAVE as $F49E/$F5DD; this machine runs 901227-03, whose
defaults are $F4A5/$F5ED, and those are the values present.

CASSETTE_BUFFER (TBUFFER, $033C-$03FB) - the KERNAL's 192-byte datasette block buffer.
Unused by a disk-only program, which is exactly why the game parks its resident loader
trampoline RUN_FASTLOADER at $03A0, inside this buffer: 192 bytes that neither BASIC nor the
KERNAL will disturb as long as no tape operation occurs. $033C-$039F is still zero-filled;
the game's code begins at $03A0.

RUN_FASTLOADER ($03A0)
Purpose: Bring the parked custom disk fast-loader into executable space and run it. The image normally lives in the RAM hidden beneath the CIA/I-O window at $DC00-$DFFF; this wrapper exchanges it with the four screen-matrix pages at $CC00-$CFFF and then calls it at $CC00.
Inputs: None in registers. Requires the loader image parked in RAM under $DC00-$DFFF and KERNAL file parameters already set by the caller (LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART performs SETNAM before calling).
Outputs: The requested part has been loaded by the custom loader; the loader image and the previous screen-matrix contents have been exchanged back by the callee's second half, so $CC00-$CFFF again holds the loader image only for the duration of the call.
Assumptions: Entry with $01=$37 so that KERNAL ROM and the I/O page are visible; the four exchange pages exist both at $CC00-$CFFF and in RAM under $DC00-$DFFF.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, plus whatever the custom loader itself uses; the visible screen matrix is destroyed for the duration of the call.
Hardware changes: Indirect: the callee SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE drives the 6510 port $01 between $37 and $38, and the loader itself drives the serial bus on CIA 2 port A ($DD00). The text screen is unreadable while the loader occupies $CC00-$CFFF, which is why the caller blanks the VIC display first.
Swap the hidden loader into execution space.
Execute the custom loader now resident at $CC00.

SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE ($03A6)
Purpose: Exchange the four 256-byte pages at $CC00-$CFFF with the four pages of RAM that lie underneath the I/O window at $DC00-$DFFF, so that a program parked in hidden RAM becomes executable and the displaced screen matrix is preserved.
Inputs: None in registers. Requires four consecutive pages at $CC00 and four underneath $DC00.
Outputs: The two four-page regions have swapped contents. All four self-modified absolute operand high bytes ($03AD, $03B0, $03B3, $03B7) are reset to $CC/$DC so the routine is re-entrant across calls. Returns with interrupts disabled.
Assumptions: Entry with $01=$37. The routine reaches $38 by INC $01, which is only correct from $37; it restores by DEC $01. Interrupts must stay off while I/O is hidden, otherwise an IRQ acknowledging $D019 would write RAM instead.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the four operand bytes named above, and the interrupt-disable flag (left set on return).
Hardware changes: Executes SEI. Changes the 6510 on-chip port $01 from $37 to $38, which unmaps the whole I/O page (VIC-II, SID, CIAs, colour RAM) and exposes the RAM beneath it, then restores $37. No device register is written.
Increment $01 from $37 to $38: expose RAM at $D000-$DFFF.
Read one byte from the visible $CCxx page; operand high byte advances per page.
High operand byte of LDY $CC00,X at $03AB. The exchange loop advances it through pages $CC-$CF, reads parked loader pages $DC-$DF, and swaps the bytes; it resets to $CC on exit.
Read the corresponding byte from RAM hidden beneath I/O.
High operand byte of LDA $DC00,X at $03AE, advanced through $DC-$DF and restored to $DC after the four-page loader exchange.
Move hidden-RAM byte into the $CCxx loader page.
High operand byte of STA $CC00,X at $03B1, advanced alongside the visible source operand through $CC-$CF and restored to $CC on exit.
Store former $CCxx byte under I/O, completing the swap.

High operand byte of STA $DC00,X at $03B5. Each byte writes the previous visible screen value beneath I/O. The loop ends when this operand reaches $E0, restores processor port $37, resets all four page operands, and returns at $03E0.
Advance the $CCxx read operand to the next page.
Advance the $DCxx read operand to the next page.
Advance the $CCxx write operand to the next page.
Advance the $DCxx write operand to the next page.
Stop after swapping through page $DF.
Restore $01 from $38 to $37 so ROM and I/O are visible again.
Reset all self-modified operand high bytes for the next invocation.

31 zero bytes. $03E1-$03FB is the tail of the KERNAL's cassette buffer ($033C-$03FB) and
$03FC-$03FF is documented as unused; RUN_FASTLOADER / SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE ends with RTS at
$03E0 and nothing follows it.
The game parks its fast-loader wrapper at $03A0-$03E0 for the usual C64 reason: on a
disk-only program the tape buffer is free RAM, and it stays visible in every $01 banking
configuration, including the all-RAM map the swap routine selects. The zeros here are the
KERNAL RAMTAS boot fill.

DISK_SAVE_GAME ($0494)
Purpose: Complete but unreachable KERNAL save-game implementation: copy the save start address into the KERNAL's zero-page pointer at $FE/$FF, set the file parameters, and SAVE from there up to DISK_SAVE_END_ADDR.
Inputs: DISK_LOAD_ADDR ($28BB/$28BC) is the start of the block to write; DISK_SAVE_END_ADDR ($28BD/$28BE) is the exclusive end; FILENAME_BUF holds the eight-character name.

TOKEN_POINTERS_TABLE — 94 little-endian pointers, one per compressed-text dictionary token.
A prose byte with bit 7 set is a token reference: the renderer clears bit 7, doubles the
remaining 0..93 id and reads the word at TOKEN_POINTERS_TABLE + 2*id. The pointer addresses a
dictionary record, so ids $80-$DD are defined and $DE-$FF have no entry in this occupant.
The 94 pointers occupy $25DD-$2698; the records they address begin immediately afterwards at
$2699 (WORD_THE_LC) and run to $28B8.

Compressed-text dictionary records, $2699-$28B8. Each record is one length byte followed by
exactly that many ASCII characters, with no terminator and no padding; records are packed back
to back and are reached only through TOKEN_POINTERS_TABLE ($25DD), never by scanning.
The dictionary stores case-sensitive duplicates because prose is emitted verbatim: "the"
($2699) and "The" ($27CF), "to" ($26DB) and "To" ($2805), "There" ($26AB) and "there" ($2730),
"You" ($26D3) and "you" ($28B5) are separate tokens. Labels ending _LC or _CAP mark the
lower-case or capitalised member of such a pair.

BLIT_ROOM_GRAPHIC processes one character row at a time. For width W it copies W*8 bitmap bytes to BITMAP_ROW_ADDR_TABLE[row]+column*8, W screen bytes to SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_TABLE[row]+column, and W colour bytes to COLOR_ROW_ADDR_TABLE[row]+column. Thus each cell costs eight bitmap bytes, one screen byte, and one colour byte.
RASTER_SPLIT_PICTURE selects VIC bank 3, multicolor bitmap mode, screen matrix $CC00, bitmap $E000, and colour RAM $D800. Each two-bit pixel chooses $D021, the screen-byte high nybble, the screen-byte low nybble, or the colour-RAM low nybble. This explains both the interleaving and the ten-byte-per-cell stride.

ZERO_PAGE_BACKUP ($A000-$A0FF) - the game's shadow copy of zero page, swapped in and out
around KERNAL calls by SWAP_ZERO_PAGE_AND_BACKUP ($053C).
The game keeps its own working variables in zero page, which the KERNAL also uses. Rather
than saving individual locations, $053C exchanges the two 256-byte images wholesale: for each
index it loads the live byte, loads the backup byte, writes the backup value live, and writes
the live value into the backup. One routine therefore serves both directions - calling it
twice restores the original state - and there is no separate "restore" entry point.
053C  LDY #$FF
053E  LDA $0000,Y     ; live zero-page byte
0541  TAX
0542  LDA $A000,Y     ; corresponding backup byte
0545  STA $0000,Y     ; backup -> live
0548  TXA
0549  STA $A000,Y     ; live -> backup
054C  DEY
054D  CPY #$01        ; stop before index $01
054F  BNE $053E
C64 SPECIFIC, AND THE REASON FOR THE ODD LOOP BOUND: the loop runs Y = $FF down to $02 and
deliberately never touches $0000 and $0001. On a 6510 those two addresses are not RAM but the
CPU's on-chip I/O port - $0001 is the bank-select register that decides whether BASIC, KERNAL,
I/O or RAM is visible at $A000-$BFFF and $D000-$FFFF, and $0000 is its data-direction
register. Swapping a stale value into $0001 would change the memory map underneath the
running code, most likely unmapping the very routine performing the swap. Banking is managed
separately, by explicit stores to $01 (see $975D, which restores the game's standard $36 map
after a disk load).
Note the backup lives at $A000-$BFFF RAM, i.e. underneath the BASIC ROM image, which is
exactly the region the $01 value chosen by this game leaves as RAM.
The instruction operands establish the $A000 base. Ghidra records an `abs,Y` reference one byte above the base, so operand inspection is required. Byte evidence agrees: aligning $A000 with $0000 matches 198 of 256 captured bytes, against 80 when aligned at $A001. The 58 differences are expected because the backup is a prior zero-page snapshot, not a live mirror.

C64 DISPLAY SEMANTICS (for a reader fluent in 6510 but not in VIC-II)
The picture band runs in multicolor bitmap mode: RASTER_SPLIT_PICTURE ($A7E3) sets $D011=$3B
(BMM=1, bitmap mode), $D016=$D8 (MCM=1, multicolor), $D018=$38 (video matrix $CC00, bitmap

pixel, so horizontal resolution halves - each 8x8 cell is 4 double-wide pixels across - and the
colour of a pixel is selected by the bit pair:
00 -> background register $D021
01 -> high nybble of that cell's screen-matrix byte
10 -> low  nybble of that cell's screen-matrix byte
11 -> low  nybble of that cell's colour-RAM byte
Hence the 4 screen bytes and 4 colour bytes per row: they carry three of the four palette
entries for the four cells in that row. An icon is 32 x 32 screen pixels (16 double-wide
multicolor pixels wide).

Purpose: The gameplay interrupt handler, installed in the KERNAL RAM vector CINV. A CLC followed by a BCC whose offset byte at $A7E2 is self-modified selects one of the three raster-split phase bodies, so successive interrupts cycle picture, text and bottom.

Hardware changes: Through the selected phase: VIC-II $D011, $D016, $D018, $D021, $D012 and $D019. CINV itself is not modified here.

Purpose: Hand the machine back to the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs in a state a stock C64 can survive: select a ROM-visible memory map, zero the low RAM pages, rebuild the KERNAL indirect vector block, re-run BASIC's vector and zero-page initialisation, and restore the stock IRQ handler.

Purpose: Point the KERNAL RAM interrupt vector at the game's raster-split dispatcher and stop CIA 1 from raising its own interrupt. The exact inverse of the tail of RESTORE_SYSTEM_TO_BASIC.
Inputs: None. Also located inside a dead object-icon slot.
Outputs: CINV ($0314/$0315) = $A7E0; CIA 1's FLAG interrupt mask cleared; any latched CIA 1 interrupt request discarded.
Assumptions: Requires $01=$36 so that $A7E0 is the game's handler in RAM rather than BASIC ROM, and requires the raster source and initial compare to have been configured already. Writes $10 to CIA 1 interrupt control $DC0D: with bit 7 clear the one bits are cleared, so this clears the FLAG mask and leaves the other sources alone.
